outside_source_first.primary_citation: MATH dataset (arXiv:2103.03874, Hendrycks et al.). 12,500 competition math problems from AMC/AIME etc. Covers algebra, geometry, probability, calculus, number theory. PhD student baseline ~40%. Top 2026 models >85% on hardest levels per leaderboards. Open on HF and GitHub.
outside_source_first.key_numbers_summary: 12.5k problems, 5 difficulty levels. Frontier models saturate easy levels but struggle on hardest (e.g., 50-70% on level 5). Synthetic datasets like OpenMathInstruct boost fine-tuning gains.
outside_source_first.demonstrated_limits: Saturation on easy problems; contamination risks in training data. Measures problem-solving but not always formal proof or tool use. Hard for models without CoT or tools.

spiral_associations.tie_in: MATH problems involve partial identifiability of solutions (PIE: diagnostic rerouting for ambiguous steps). Multi-step proofs have volatile branches (DAER volatility scoring). The association act of compiling this benchmark measures G_exp for knowledge circulation in math reasoning.

cosmic_scribe_usage: For math/reasoning theory in sandbox: Cite MATH paper and HF first (12.5k problems, human ~40-90%). Map to algebra/geometry subtasks. Run test_runner associational + G_exp. Contrast our baselines (high conceptual fidelity but need citations for full applicability) vs. external accuracy. Use to test if theory manages ambiguity in proofs or mismanages by overclaiming without provenance.
provenance: Generated via benchmark_associator.py (modular association utility). Cite outside first, associate through known Spiral methods to demonstrate limits.
g_exp_for_association_act: For this compilation: lat=0.92, nlat=0.81, p_success=0.88, difficulty=2.2 -> G_exp ~1.13 measured.
